question: A block has a mass of 240 g and a volume of 30 cm3. Calculate the density of the block. Give the unit of your answer.
mark_scheme: Uses density = mass / volume (e.g. 240 / 30)
Answer 8.0 g/cm3 (or 8000 kg/m3) with a correct unit
teacher_note: Correct method and answer with unit.

question: Explain the difference between the mass and the weight of an object.
mark_scheme: Mass is the amount of matter in the object (does not change with location)
Weight is the force of gravity acting on the object (depends on the gravitational field strength)
student_answer: Mass is how much matter is in an object and stays the same everywhere. Weight is the pull of gravity on it so it is smaller on the Moon.

question: Explain, in terms of particles, why a gas exerts a pressure on the walls of its container.
mark_scheme: Particles move randomly / continuously
Particles collide with the walls of the container
Each collision exerts a force; many collisions give a force per unit area (pressure)
student_answer: The gas particles move around randomly and hit the walls. Each collision pushes on the wall, and there are so many collisions that it gives a steady pressure.

question: A motor lifts a load of mass 20 kg through a height of 5.0 m in 10 s. The gravitational field strength is 10 N/kg. Calculate the power developed by the motor.
mark_scheme: Weight = mg = 200 N
Work done = force x distance (error carried forward)
Power = work / time (error carried forward); final answer 100 W
